sections.html:
Billing and payment sit with the tax collector. Values and exemptions belong to the appraiser, while appeals and tax deed auctions run through the clerk's office. A call to the wrong office costs time.

The tax collector's mailing address is 3291 Tamiami Trail East, Naples, FL 34112. Property tax questions go to propertytax@colliertax.com or 239-252-8171. The Property Appraiser can be reached at (239) 252-8141 for value and exemption questions.

sections.h2: Early payment discounts and late dates
sections.html:
Bills are payable in November, and paying early earns a discount that shrinks monthly: 4% in November, down a point each month to 1% in February. The gross amount is due in March, and the bill goes delinquent in April.

Collier County payment months
Month paidDiscount
November4% off
December3% off
January2% off
February1% off
MarchGross amount due
AprilDelinquent

The collector doesn't accept post-dated checks. Certificate sales on unpaid items finish by June 1. Offices close on listed holidays, including Thanksgiving and the day after, and on one training day in October.

The appraiser values every parcel as of each New Year's Day. In mid-August the appraiser mails a TRIM notice, the formal proposal of next year's tax.

  • August: TRIM notice arrives, listing proposed values and tax.
  • September and October: local taxing authorities hold budget hearings.
  • November: the tax collector sends bills.

Other property faces a 10 percent yearly ceiling on assessed growth. Read the TRIM notice closely, because it starts the appeal clock.

Petitions go to the Value Adjustment Board, whose clerk is the Collier County clerk and comptroller. An assessment appeal is due within 25 days after the appraiser mails the TRIM notice, which usually lands in mid-September.

Other petitions run on different clocks. The clerk's table lists these:

  • Exemption or classification denial: 30 days after the appraiser mails the denial, with all denials mailed by July 1
  • Tax deferral denial: 30 days after the tax collector mails the denial
  • Portability and change of ownership or control: 25 days after the TRIM notice

The filing fee is $50.00 per petition per parcel for most types and $15.00 for a portability petition. The board has two county commissioners, one school board member and two citizen members, and special magistrates hear the cases and recommend decisions. Late filing needs a good cause statement.

The tax collector bills ad valorem tax, meaning tax according to worth, on real estate and on a business's tangible personal property. One mill equals a dollar of tax on each thousand dollars of taxable value, and every taxing authority sets its own rate, so the county, school district, city and special districts all appear on one bill.

Run three checks before you pay or sell:

  • Match the parcel number and legal owner on the bill to your deed.
  • Confirm the homestead exemption shows on the bill if you applied by March 1.
  • See whether any non-ad valorem charge appears, because those are assessments rather than value-based tax.

The tax collector's site links to a tax search where you can pull a notice or receipt, and a mortgage lender that pays from escrow should still be checked against that record.

Homestead applications reach the appraiser by March 1, and the house must be your permanent home on January 1. The exemption reaches $50,000: the first $25,000 reduces every levy, school tax included, and the next $25,000 reduces only non-school levies on value above $50,000.

Under Save Our Homes, a homestead's assessed value may climb each year by the smaller of 3 percent and the CPI change, and the state's chart prints 2.7% for 2026. After a sale the parcel goes back to full market-based value the next New Year's Day, which can make a buyer's bill very different from the seller's. Portability lets an owner bring accumulated savings along to a replacement Florida home, provided it begins inside a three-year window after the old one ended.

Homestead protection ends if the home is rented or stops being the permanent residence. Senior owners may qualify for added local exemptions, and disabled former servicemembers have separate benefits. The appraiser can say which apply to your Naples or Marco Island address.

Both are listed on the tax collector's property tax page. Deferring homestead tax takes Form DR-570, filed with the collector by March 31 after the assessment year, and covers the part above 5 percent of household income.

A permanent resident 65 or older may defer the part above 3 percent. The installment plan under section 197.222 needs an application by the May 1 cutoff in the year of assessment. Confirm current terms with the collector, since deferred tax accrues interest and carries a lien.

sections.h2: Who settles the tax at a sale
sections.html:
Unpaid current-year tax is settled at closing, normally by the closing agent from the proceeds. Request a payoff figure for your closing date, and confirm earlier years show paid.

If taxes stay unpaid, the county sells a certificate. Once two years have run from the April 1 following issue, the holder can file for a tax deed, and the clerk then runs the auction. A homestead parcel's opening bid adds one-half of the latest assessment. At the clerk's auction, a winning bidder pays within 24 hours, so a delinquent house can be lost quickly, and a seller with unpaid years should settle them before listing. For recording costs on your own sale, see the Collier County property records guide.

On closing day, compare the title agent's tax lines with the collector's payoff and keep the receipt.

The Collier Clerk posts both a tax deeds list and a foreclosure sale list on its records search page. The tax deeds list covers properties where the tax collector sold certificates for delinquent real estate taxes.

The collector awards each certificate to the bidder who accepts the lowest interest rate, in quarter-percent steps, and unsold certificates go to the county at the maximum rate. The holder may not contact the owner for payment until two years from the first April 1 after issue. A homeowner with a small delinquency has options before then, since payment to the tax collector redeems the certificate. Ask the collector's office for a payoff early rather than waiting for a sale notice.

faqs.q: What date marks Collier County tax as late?
faqs.a: April 1. The gross amount is due in March, with discounts only from November through February.

faqs.q: What early-payment discounts does Collier County offer?
faqs.a: Savings shrink from 4% in November to 1% in February. After that the full gross amount applies, starting in March.

faqs.q: How long is the window to contest a Collier County assessment?
faqs.a: Petitions are due within 25 days after the appraiser mails the TRIM notice. Most petitions carry a $50.00 filing fee.

faqs.q: Does Collier County accept post-dated checks for property tax?
faqs.a: No. The tax collector doesn't accept post-dated checks for property tax bills.

faqs.q: What is the mailing address for Collier County tax payments?
faqs.a: Mail it to the Collier County Tax Collector, 3291 Tamiami Trail East, Naples, FL 34112. Questions go to 239-252-8171.
